q: By what date must the Sangguniang Barangay approve the BAIP by resolution?
e: The BAIP is prepared within May and approved on or before June 7, before the Budget Call.

q: Who prepares the Barangay Annual Investment Program (BAIP)?
o: The Punong Barangay, assisted by the Barangay Secretary and Treasurer
e: The PB prepares the BAIP with the Secretary and Treasurer, then submits it to the SB.

q: In the BAIP reference code, which sector code is used for Social Services?
e: 1000 General Public Services, 3000 Social Services, 8000 Economic Services, 9000 Other Services.

q: The BAIP is what portion of the Barangay Development Investment Program (BDIP)?
e: The BAIP is the one-year slice of the three-year BDIP and links the plan to the budget.

q: The Barangay Development Plan (BDP) covers how many years?
e: The BDP is a three-year multi-sectoral plan initiated by the BDC and approved by the SB.

q: What share of the Barangay Development Council must be CSO/NGO representatives?
e: CSO/NGO representatives constitute not less than one-fourth of the fully organized council.

q: The Budget Call of the Punong Barangay is based on which document?
e: The Budget Call is issued based on the approved BAIP, the LGC and the Manual.

q: By when do the City/Municipal Treasurer and Accountant issue the joint certified statement of income for the barangay?
e: The joint certified statement is issued on or before September 5.

q: Which is one of the three parts of the Barangay Expenditure Program (BEP)?
e: The BEP has a Receipts Program, an Expenditure Program and General Provisions.

q: Which form is the Statement of Indebtedness submitted with the BEP?
e: BBP Form No. 4 is the Statement of Indebtedness; Form No. 3 is the Plantilla of Personnel.

q: The Plantilla of Personnel is which budget preparation form?
e: BBP Form No. 3 is the Plantilla of Personnel.

q: The aggregate amount proposed in the BEP must not exceed:
e: Section 324(a), LGC: the aggregate amount appropriated may not exceed the estimates of income.

q: What is the minimum share of the annual NTA appropriated for development projects?
e: At least 20% of the NTA must be appropriated for development projects. More than 20% is allowed.

q: Which may be charged against the 20% Development Fund?
o: Construction of a barangay health station
e: PS, administrative expenses, travel, training fees and admin furniture or vehicles are on the negative list.

q: How much of the general fund is set aside for the Sangguniang Kabataan?
e: The SK share is 10% of the general fund, appropriated in lump sum.

q: What percentage of the BDRRMF is the Quick Response Fund?
e: Of the BDRRMF, 30% is QRF and 70% is for prevention, preparedness, response, rehabilitation and recovery.

q: The BDRRMF is at least what share of estimated revenue from regular sources?
e: Not less than 5% of estimated regular revenue is set aside as BDRRMF (RA 10121).

q: Appropriation for debt servicing may not exceed what share of regular income?
e: The debt service cap is 20% of the regular income of the barangay.

q: The PS limitation is what share of income realized from local sources in the next preceding fiscal year?
e: Total PS appropriations may not exceed 55% of income actually realized from local sources.

q: Discretionary funds of the Punong Barangay may not exceed what share of actual basic RPT receipts of the next preceding calendar year?
e: Annual discretionary appropriations may not exceed 2% of actual receipts from basic real property tax.

q: What share of the total barangay budget goes to GAD programs at minimum?
e: At least 5% of the total budget corresponds to GAD PPAs, attributed to existing programs.

q: The programs of the Local Council for the Protection of Children get what share of the barangay's NTA?
e: One percent of the NTA is allocated for LCPC programs.

q: Salaries of Barangay Economic Enterprise employees are charged to:
e: BEE PS is charged to the enterprise budget and excluded from the barangay PS limit.

q: Excess income of a BEE, after costs and the return of advances or loans, goes to:
o: The General Fund of the barangay
e: Costs are deducted first, then advances returned, and any excess forms part of the General Fund.

q: The creation of new positions and salary increases may in no case be:
e: Section 325(g), LGC: creation of positions and salary increases are not made retroactive.

q: The BEP is submitted to the Sangguniang Barangay not later than:
e: Section 318, LGC: the executive budget is submitted not later than October 16.

q: BBP Form No. 6 is which document?
e: Form No. 5 is the Statement of Funding Sources; Form No. 6 the Statement of Supplemental Appropriation.

q: In times of public calamity, a supplemental budget may be funded by:
e: Realignment of appropriations is allowed in times of public calamity.

q: Savings include:
e: Savings include unobligated compensation for vacant positions and leaves without pay.

q: An Appropriation Ordinance is enacted upon the affirmative vote of:
o: A majority of all SB members
e: Any ordinance authorizing payment of money needs a majority of all members duly elected and qualified.

q: The Sangguniang Barangay may not increase amounts or add items in the BEP, except to provide for:
e: Additions are limited to statutory and contractual obligations, within the total of the executive budget.

q: The Barangay Secretary must post the AO within how many days after approval?
e: Posting is required not later than five days after approval (Sec. 59(b), LGC).

q: The ordinance enacting the annual budget takes effect:
o: At the beginning of the ensuing calendar year
On the day it is posted
On the date the BAC meets
e: The annual budget takes effect at the start of the ensuing calendar year; a supplemental budget upon approval.

q: Copies of the AO are furnished to the SP/SB within:
e: Section 333(a), LGC: within 10 days from approval, through the city or municipal budget officer.

q: The SP/SB reviews the barangay AO within:
e: The SP/SB has 60 days; if no action is taken the AO continues in full force and effect.

q: Which causes the AO to be declared inoperative in its entirety?
o: Aggregate appropriations exceed estimates of income
e: Appropriations beyond estimated income make the whole AO inoperative; GAD deficiency is a condition.

q: If PS appropriations exceed the 55% limit, the AO is:
o: Returned to the PB for reenactment
e: The excess over the PS limitation is disallowed, making the AO inoperative in part.

q: A deficient GAD budget in the AO is typically cited as:
e: Deficiency in budgetary requirements by attribution is cited as a condition.

q: Under a reenacted budget, the barangay may NOT:
e: Only existing salaries, statutory and contractual obligations and essential operating expenses are reenacted.

q: The ARO for Capital Outlays is which form?
e: ARO forms: No. 1 PS, No. 2 MOOE, No. 3 CO, No. 4 Financial Expenses.

q: An allotment is:
o: An authorization issued by the PB allowing a unit to incur obligations within its appropriation
e: An allotment allows obligations up to a specific amount within the appropriation.

q: Augmentation from savings is recorded on which form?
e: BBE Form No. 7 is the Augmentation Form.

q: BBE Form No. 5 must be prepared within how many days after the AO is approved?
e: Detailed Financial and Physical Performance Targets are prepared within seven days after approval.

q: Total disbursements from a fund may not exceed actual collections plus what share of uncollected estimated revenue?
e: Section 337, LGC: actual collections plus 50% of uncollected estimated revenue.

q: The Quarterly Report of Receipts (BBAc Form 1) is due on or before:
o: The 10th day of the month after the quarter
e: BBAc Forms 1 to 3 are submitted on or before the 10th day of the month following the quarter.

q: The semestral Budget Performance Report (BBAc Form 4) is due on or before:
o: The 15th day of the month after the semester
The last day of the year
e: It is jointly prepared by the Treasurer and Secretary by the 15th day after each semester.

q: Accountability reports are posted in how many conspicuous places?
e: The Barangay Secretary posts reports in three conspicuous places.

q: The share of all barangays in the National Tax Allotment is:
e: NTA: provinces 23%, cities 23%, municipalities 34%, barangays 20%.

q: The minimum NTA share per barangay with at least 100 inhabitants is:
e: Each eligible barangay gets a minimum of ₱80,000 a year.

q: After the minimum, the remaining barangay NTA is distributed:
e: The balance goes 60% on population and 40% equal sharing.

q: Barangay share of national wealth proceeds where resources are within a province:
e: Province 20%, component city/municipality 45%, barangay 35%.

q: Who has direct responsibility to design, install, implement and monitor the barangay internal control system?
e: The Punong Barangay is directly responsible for the system of internal control.

q: Which is one of the four risk responses in internal control?
e: The responses are transfer, tolerate, terminate and treat.

q: BHW and BNS honoraria may not exceed the minimum salary of which grade?
e: BHWs and BNS may receive honoraria not exceeding the SG-4 minimum rate.

q: Honoraria for tanods and Lupong Tagapamayapa members may not exceed the minimum salary of which grade?
e: Per LBC No. 63, the total may not exceed the minimum rate of SG-1.

q: Barangay officials are entitled to which instead of terminal leave benefits?
o: Cumulation and commutation of leave credits
e: Leave credits cumulate up to one year and are commuted yearly.

q: Can a barangay pass an augmentation ordinance while operating under a reenacted budget?
o: No, there is no approved annual budget
e: Savings and augmentation require an approved annual budget for the current year.

q: What is the Small Value Procurement (SVP) threshold for barangays?
e: Section 34.2 sets the SVP ceiling for barangays at ₱100,000.

q: Under SVP, how many suppliers must receive the RFQ?
e: The BAC sends RFQs to at least three suppliers; receiving one quotation is enough to evaluate.

q: For SVP with an ABC above ₱200,000, the RFQ is posted for:
e: RFQ/RFP is posted for three calendar days on PhilGEPS, the entity website and a conspicuous place.

q: Direct Acquisition covers goods and services with an ABC not exceeding:
e: Direct Acquisition allows purchase from known reputable sources up to ₱200,000 without canvass.

q: A Repeat Order must be availed of within how long from the notice to proceed of the original contract?
e: Repeat Order must be within six months from the NTP of the original contract.

q: A Repeat Order may not exceed what share of the original contract quantity of each item?
e: Repeat Orders are capped at 25% of the quantity of each item and need at least four units per item.

q: Negotiated Procurement after failed biddings requires how many failures?
e: After a second failure of bidding the entity may resort to negotiated procurement.

q: After two failed biddings, the ABC may be increased by not more than:
o: 20% of the ABC of the last failed bidding
e: The BAC may revise the ABC, but not by more than 20% of the last failed bidding's ABC.

q: Which is a ground for Negotiated Procurement (emergency)?
o: Imminent danger to life or property during a state of calamity
e: Emergency cases include imminent danger to life or property during a state of calamity.

q: How many modes of procurement are listed in Section 26 of the IRR?
e: The IRR lists eleven modes, from Competitive Bidding to Direct Procurement for STI.

q: Which items are NOT procurement activities under the Act?
o: Engagement of Contract of Service and Job Order workers
e: COS and JO engagement, direct assistance to beneficiaries and training participation are not procurement.

q: Common-Use Supplies and Equipment (CSE) are procured from:
e: All LGUs procure CSE only from PS-DBM, subject to availability and listed exceptions.

q: The mandatory video recording of conferences applies to goods costing above:
e: Video recording applies to goods above ₱10M, infrastructure above ₱20M and consulting above ₱5M.

q: Renewal of regular and recurring services is generally limited to:
e: Each renewed contract shall not exceed one year, except office space rent and telecommunications.

q: Who prepares the Project Procurement Management Plan (PPMP)?
e: End-User or Implementing Units formulate PPMPs; the BAC Secretariat consolidates them into the APP.

q: No government procurement may be undertaken unless it is in accordance with:
o: The approved Indicative or final APP
e: Section 7.8: procurement must follow the approved Indicative APP or final APP.

q: The approved final APP must be posted and submitted to the GPPB by:
o: End of January of the budget year
End of December before the budget year
e: The final APP is posted and submitted to the GPPB on or before the end of January.

q: Market scoping is conducted:
o: As a preliminary undertaking in preparing the PPMP
e: The End-User or Implementing Unit conducts market scoping when preparing the PPMP.

q: Early Procurement Activities may proceed up to, but short of:
e: EPA is done short of award, pending approval of the funding such as the appropriation ordinance.

q: For LGUs, the Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC) is approved through:
o: An appropriation ordinance of the Sanggunian
e: For LGUs the budget for the contract is approved by the Sanggunian through an appropriation ordinance.

q: Subcontracting is limited to what share for Goods?
e: Subcontracted portion may not exceed 20% for Goods and 50% for Infrastructure Projects.

q: Splitting of government contracts is:
e: Dividing contracts to evade the Act is not allowed; procurement by lot or package is allowed.

q: A barangay BAC is composed of how many regular SB members, excluding the Punong Barangay?
e: The BAC has five or seven regular members of the Sangguniang Barangay except the PB.

q: Who designates the BAC Chairperson in a barangay?
e: The Punong Barangay, as local chief executive, designates the chair, vice-chair and members.

q: The fixed term of BAC members is:
o: Until the end of the PB's term
e: Members have a one-year term, with no more than three consecutive terms unless allowed by the HoPE.

q: A BAC quorum is a majority of members, which must include:
e: The presence of the Chairperson or Vice-Chairperson is required for a quorum.

q: The BAC Chairperson votes only:
e: The Chairperson, or in absence the Vice-Chairperson, votes only in case of a tie.

q: BAC honoraria may not exceed what share of basic monthly salary?
e: Honoraria for BAC, TWG and ad hoc Secretariat are capped at 30% of basic monthly salary.

q: The BAC must invite at least how many observers?
o: Two, apart from the COA representative
e: At least two observers: one from a private group and one from a CSO or PO.

q: Observers must be invited at least how many calendar days before the activity?
e: Observers are invited in writing at least five calendar days before the stage.

q: If observers submit no report within seven days after the activity, it is presumed that:
o: The BAC followed the correct procedure
e: Absence of a report within seven calendar days creates a presumption of proper procedure.

q: A pre-bid conference is mandatory for projects with an ABC of:
e: The BAC shall conduct at least one pre-bid conference for ABC of ₱3M or more.

q: The pre-bid conference is held at least how many days before the bid deadline?
e: It is held at least 12 calendar days before the deadline, not earlier than 7 days from posting.

q: Supplemental Bid Bulletins amending Bidding Documents are issued at least how many days before bids are due?
e: Bid Bulletins are issued at least seven calendar days before the deadline.

q: The maximum period from posting of the ITB to receipt of bids for Goods is:
e: For Goods, a maximum of 45 calendar days from the last day of posting.

q: Bids submitted after the deadline are:
e: Late bids are not accepted and are recorded in the minutes.

q: Bids and bid securities are valid for no more than:
e: Bid validity may not exceed 120 calendar days from the date of bid opening.

q: Bid security in cash or cashier's check must be at least what share of the ABC?
e: Cash or cashier's or manager's check requires 2% of the ABC; bank guarantee or surety bond 5%.

q: Which is an acceptable form of bid security?
e: Bidding Documents must include a Bid Securing Declaration among at least three forms of bid security.

q: A bid price higher than the ABC results in:
e: The ABC is the ceiling; bids above it are automatically disqualified.

q: Bid evaluation for the Lowest Calculated Bid must be completed within:
o: Seven calendar days from the bid deadline
e: Evaluation under LCB is completed within seven calendar days.

q: In MEARB evaluation, the price proposal is weighted at:
e: The price proposal is given a minimum weight of 15% up to 40%.

q: After notice, the bidder with the lowest bid submits post-qualification documents within:
e: The bidder submits eligibility documents within five calendar days from notice.

q: Post-qualification is completed in not more than:
e: The BAC completes post-qualification within 12 days, extendable to an aggregate of 45 days for Goods.

q: From bid opening to award, the process shall not exceed:
e: Section 67: the process from opening of bids to award shall not exceed 60 calendar days.

q: The HoPE approves or disapproves the BAC recommendation to award within:
e: The HoPE has not more than ten calendar days from the BAC recommendation to act.

q: After the Notice of Award, the winning bidder posts performance security and signs the contract within:
e: Documents, performance security and contract signing must be completed within ten calendar days.

q: Performance security in cash for Goods is not less than:
e: For Goods and Consulting Services 5%; Infrastructure Projects 10%; surety bond 30%.

q: Failure of bidding is declared when:
o: No bid qualifies as the lowest calculated responsive bid
The bid is below the ABC
e: Failure of bidding includes no bids received, all ineligible, or no bid qualifying as responsive.

q: A request for reconsideration of a BAC decision is filed within:
e: The bidder files within three days; the BAC decides within seven days.

q: After a denied request for reconsideration, a protest to the HoPE is filed within:
e: The protest is filed within seven days from receipt of the denial.

q: For LGUs, the HoPE decision on protests is final for Goods of:
e: For LGUs, finality applies to Goods up to ₱1.25M, infrastructure up to ₱12.5M and consulting up to ₱2.5M.

q: Liquidated damages are at least what share of the unperformed portion per day of delay?
e: The rate is at least 1/10 of 1% of the cost of the unperformed portion for every day of delay.

q: When liquidated damages reach what share of the contract price may the entity terminate?
e: Once cumulative liquidated damages reach 10% of the contract price, the entity may terminate.

q: Cumulative positive Variation Orders for infrastructure are limited to:
e: Positive Variation Orders may not exceed 10%, and up to 20% only in exceptional cases.

q: Advance payment for Infrastructure Projects may not exceed:
e: Advance payment is up to 15% with an irrevocable standby letter of credit, bank guarantee or surety bond.

q: Retention money on infrastructure progress payments is:
e: Progress payments are subject to 10% retention until 50% of the works are completed.

q: The warranty period for Non-expendable Supplies is at least:
e: Warranty is three months for expendable and one year for non-expendable supplies.

q: The structural defects warranty for permanent structures runs for:
e: Permanent structures 15 years, semi-permanent 5 years, other structures 2 years.

q: Suspension for the first offense lasts:
e: Suspension is one year for the first offense and two years for the second.

q: Blacklisting with perpetual disqualification applies after:
o: A third offense imposed with blacklisting
e: A third offense, or a combination of three blacklisting violations, brings perpetual disqualification.

q: Relation of a bidder to BAC members within what degree results in automatic disqualification?
e: Bidders must swear they are not related to the HoPE, BAC, TWG and others up to the third civil degree.

q: The PhilGEPS Certificate of Registration (Platinum Membership) is effective for:
e: The Certificate is effective for one year and may be renewed or updated.

q: The Single Largest Completed Contract (SLCC) for Goods must be at least what share of the ABC?
e: The bidder must have completed within ten years an SLCC at least 50% of the ABC.

q: Domestic preference applies if the domestic bid is not more than what share above the lowest foreign bid?
e: The entity awards to the domestic bidder if its bid is not more than 25% in excess of the lowest foreign bid.

q: The barangay fiscal year runs from:
e: For accounting purposes the fiscal year starts January 1 and ends December 31.

q: Barangay accounts are kept under which system?
e: Barangay accounts are kept under a double-entry bookkeeping system.

q: Who maintains the books of accounts of a barangay?
e: The Journal of Cash Transactions, General Journal, General Ledger and Subsidiary Ledgers are kept by the C/M Accountant.

q: Non-cash transactions are recorded in the:
o: General Journal through a Journal Voucher
e: Cash transactions go to the JCT; non-cash to the GJ through a JV.

q: The Cashbook is maintained and updated:
e: A Cashbook is maintained and updated daily.

q: Funds granted to a barangay for a specific purpose are recognized as:
e: Specific-purpose grants are recognized as Special Trust Fund.

q: Unspent current-year LDRRMF at year-end is transferred to:
e: Unspent LDRRMF is recorded as Special Trust Fund and tracked in the RSTF.

q: Which record tracks each Special Trust Fund until fully used?
e: An RSTF is maintained for each STF until fully utilized.

q: Who maintains the Record of Appropriations and Obligations (RAO)?
o: The Chairman of the Committee on Appropriations
e: The CCA records appropriations and obligations in the RAO.

q: Which is a separate RAO required?
e: Separate RAOs are kept for 10% SK, 5% LDRRMF, 20% Development Fund and continuing appropriations.

q: The CCA reports appropriations and balances to the PB and SB through the:
o: Statement of Appropriations, Obligations and Balances
e: The SAOB is prepared monthly and certified correct by the CCA.

q: The Record of Estimated and Actual Income (REAI) is maintained by:
e: The BT maintains it monthly and submits it to the C/M Accountant at year-end.

q: Which is the Official Receipt form used by barangays?
e: OR is Accountable Form No. 51; Real Property Tax Receipt is Form No. 56.

q: Temporary or provisional receipts:
o: May not be issued to acknowledge collections
May be issued for amounts under ₱500
e: Temporary or provisional receipts shall not be issued.

q: Official receipts are issued:
e: ORs are issued in strict numerical sequence, without erasures or alterations.

q: Barangay collections are deposited intact:
e: Collections are deposited intact daily; if the bank is over a day away, weekly or once collections reach ₱5,000.

q: Where travel time to the bank exceeds one day, deposits are made at least weekly or when collections reach:
e: Deposit weekly or as soon as collections reach ₱5,000.

q: As deputized collector of the city or municipality, the BT remits collections daily or once they reach:
e: Collections are remitted intact to the C/M Treasurer daily or at ₱5,000.

q: How many depository accounts may a barangay maintain with the AGDB?
e: The barangay maintains only one depository account in its name with the AGDB.

q: Only checks payable to whom are accepted as payment to the barangay?
e: Only checks in the name of the barangay are accepted.

q: Collections may NOT be used to:
e: Collections shall not be used to encash checks or pay barangay obligations.

q: The Report of Collections and Deposits (RCD) is submitted to the C/M Accountant on or before:
o: The 5th day of the following month
The last day of the quarter
e: BT forwards two copies of the RCD with ORs and validated deposit slips by the 5th day of the next month.

q: The Report of Bank Debit and Credit Memos is prepared by:
e: The C/M Accountant summarizes bank memos in the RBDCM and furnishes the BT a copy.

q: The monthly Bank Reconciliation Statement is prepared by:
e: The C/M Accountant prepares it upon receipt of the bank statement.

q: The Barangay Treasurer's bond is determined by the SB but not exceeding:
e: The BT shall be bonded in an amount determined by the SB not exceeding ₱10,000, with premiums paid by the barangay.

q: Barangay disbursements are generally made by:
o: Checks drawn against the depository account
e: Disbursements shall generally be made by checks drawn against the barangay depository account.

q: All check disbursements are supported with:
e: All check disbursements need a PB Certification (PBC) under oath to the bank.

q: Who signs the check and who countersigns?
e: The BT prepares and signs the check; the PB countersigns.

q: Box A of the Disbursement Voucher is certified by:
o: The Chairman of the Committee on Appropriations
e: Box A: CCA on existence of appropriation; Box B: BT on availability of funds; Box C: PB approval.

q: Box B of the Disbursement Voucher is certified by:
e: The BT certifies availability of funds and completeness of supporting documents.

q: Elected officials may be granted a cash advance only for:
e: Only permanently appointed officials may be disbursing officers; elected officials may get advances only for official travel.

q: Transfer of a cash advance from one accountable officer to another is:
e: Transfer of cash advance between accountable officers is not allowed.

q: All cash advances must be liquidated by:
e: All cash advances shall be liquidated at year-end.

q: A cash advance for payroll must be liquidated within how many days after the pay period?
e: Payroll advances are liquidated within five days after the end of the pay period.

q: A local travel cash advance is liquidated within how many days of return?
e: Liquidation is within 30 days for local travel and 60 days for foreign travel.

q: Cash advances not needed or unused for how long must be returned?
e: Advances not needed or unused for two months are returned to the collecting officer or cashier.

q: Cash advances for infrastructure projects are not granted, except for:
o: Labor payroll for projects by administration
e: No cash advance for payment on infrastructure projects except labor payroll for projects by administration.

q: Petty cash may not exceed what share of funds available to the credit of the barangay?
e: Petty cash covers one month of recurring expenses but is capped at 20% of available funds.

q: Petty cash is replenished when disbursements reach at least:
e: Replenish at 75% or as needed using a Summary of Petty Cash Disbursements.

q: The BT may directly purchase out of petty cash up to:
e: Direct purchases of not more than ₱1,000 at any time for ordinary and essential needs.

q: The petty cash fund is closed at:
e: The balance is closed at year-end and renewed using the current year's appropriation.

q: The BT submits RCDs, liquidation reports, ORs, DVs and monthly RAAF to the C/M Accountant within:
e: The BT submits within 10 days after the end of the month.

q: The C/M Accountant submits monthly collection and disbursement reports to the Auditor by:
o: The 15th working day of the next month
e: Reports go to the COA Auditor on or before the 15th working day of the succeeding month.

q: Property and supplies inventory reports are submitted not later than:
e: The PB submits year-end inventory reports by January 10.

q: Inventory costs are assigned using which method?
e: Inventory cost is assigned using the weighted (moving) average method.

q: Supplies with serviceable life of more than one year are covered by:
e: Items with more than one year of life are covered by an ICS.

q: A Property Acknowledgement Receipt must be renewed at least every:
e: PARs are renewed at least every three years or on change in custodianship.

q: Physical count of supplies and property is done:
e: The Inventory Committee conducts a count at least once a year.

q: Depreciation is computed using the straight-line method with a residual value of:
e: Straight-line depreciation after deducting residual value equivalent to 5% of cost.

q: A Request for Relief from Property Accountability for lost property is filed within:
o: 30 days from the date of loss
e: The accountable officer files the Notice of Loss and RRPA within the statutory 30 days.

q: Disposal of real property requires approval of:
e: Disposal of real property is subject to COA approval regardless of value (Sec. 380, LGC).

q: Cash overage found in a cash examination is:
o: Forfeited in favor of the government
e: Overage is forfeited in favor of the government and recorded as miscellaneous income.

q: A cash shortage is recorded as:
e: Shortage is a receivable from the accountable officer pending relief.

q: A check is stale if outstanding for over:
e: A check outstanding over six months from issue is stale; the payee is notified a month before.

q: Disallowances are recorded in the books when:
e: Disallowances are taken up only when final and executory.

q: Year-end financial statements are prepared by the C/M Accountant within:
e: The C/M Accountant prepares the statements within 60 days after the close of the year.

q: The Statement of Management Responsibility is signed by:
o: C/M Accountant, Barangay Treasurer and Punong Barangay
e: It is signed by the C/M Accountant, BT and PB.

q: The monthly Statement of Financial Performance is submitted:
o: 30 days after the close of each month
e: It is prepared monthly and submitted 30 days after month-end with a copy to the Auditor.

q: Failure to render accounts for how long is punishable under Article 218 of the Revised Penal Code?
e: A public officer who fails to render required accounts for two months is penalized.

q: Which account code is Cash - In Local Treasury?
e: Cash-In Local Treasury is 1-01-01-010; Petty Cash is 1-01-01-020.

q: Which account code is Real Property Tax revenue?
e: Real Property Tax is 4-01-01-010.

q: Which account holds taxes withheld for remittance to the BIR?
e: Withheld taxes are recorded in Due to BIR, account 2-02-01-010.

q: Biological assets are measured at:
o: Fair value less costs to sell
e: Biological assets are measured at fair value less cost to sell at recognition and each reporting date.

q: Under Section 130, collection of local taxes, fees and charges shall in no case be let to:
e: Section 130(c): the collection of local taxes, fees, charges and other impositions shall in no case be let to any private person.

q: Revenue collected under the LGC inures solely to the benefit of:
o: The local government unit levying it
e: Section 130(d): revenue inures solely to the LGU levying it, unless otherwise provided.

q: The power to impose a local tax is exercised by the sanggunian through:
e: Section 132: the taxing power is exercised through an appropriate ordinance.

q: Which tax may LGUs NOT levy, except on banks and financial institutions?
e: Section 133(a): taxing powers do not extend to income tax, except on banks and other financial institutions.

q: Local governments may NOT levy which of these?
e: Section 133(b): documentary stamp tax is outside local taxing power.

q: Barangay business tax on stores and retailers with fixed establishments is capped at what rate?
e: Section 152(a): a rate not exceeding 1% on gross sales or receipts of the preceding calendar year.

q: The barangay business tax on retailers applies where gross sales of the preceding year were ₱30,000 or less in:
e: Section 152(a): ₱50,000 or less in cities and ₱30,000 or less in municipalities.

q: A barangay clearance application must be acted upon within:
e: Section 152(c): if not issued in seven working days, the city or municipality may issue the permit.

q: Barangays may levy fees on:
o: Commercial breeding of fighting cocks and cockpits
e: Section 152(d) allows fees on cockfighting, places of recreation with admission fees and billboards.

q: Community tax proceeds collected through barangay treasurers are shared:
e: Section 164: fifty percent to the general fund of the city or municipality and fifty percent to the barangay.

q: Barangays may fine violators of tax ordinances not less than ₱100 and not more than:
e: Barangays may prescribe fines of ₱100 to ₱1,000 for violation of tax ordinances.

q: LGUs have what share in national taxes under Section 284?
e: Section 284: LGUs have a forty percent share, computed on all national taxes since FY 2022.

q: Under Section 285, barangays receive what share of the total LGU allotment?
e: Provinces 23%, cities 23%, municipalities 34%, barangays 20%.

q: At least what share of the IRA or NTA is for development projects?
e: Section 287: not less than twenty percent of the annual IRA for development projects.

q: LGUs are entitled to what share of gross national wealth collections?
e: Sections 289-290: forty percent of gross collection from utilization and development of national wealth.

q: The barangay's share of national wealth proceeds within a province is:
e: Section 292: province 20%, component city or municipality 45%, barangay 35%.

q: Proceeds from geothermal and other energy sources are applied how?
o: Eighty percent to lower the cost of electricity
e: Section 294: 80% of proceeds lowers the cost of electricity in the LGU where the source is located.

q: Section 305(a) states that no money shall be paid out of the local treasury except:
o: In pursuance of an appropriations ordinance or law
e: Section 305(a): payments require an appropriations ordinance or law.

q: Local government funds shall be spent solely for:
o: Any purpose chosen by the PB
e: Section 305(b): local government funds and monies shall be spent solely for public purposes.

q: Trust funds in the local treasury may be paid out only:
o: In fulfillment of the purpose for which the trust was created
e: Section 305(e): only for the purpose for which the trust was created or funds received.

q: Every officer who has custody of local funds shall be:
e: Section 305(f): every officer whose duties permit possession or custody of local funds shall be bonded.

q: Local budgets shall operationalize:
e: Section 305(i): local budgets shall operationalize approved local development plans.

q: Fiscal responsibility under Section 305(l) is shared by:
o: All those exercising authority over financial affairs
e: Section 305(l): fiscal responsibility is shared by all exercising authority over the financial affairs of the LGU.

q: Section 305(m) says the LGU shall endeavor to have a:
e: Section 305(m): endeavor to have a balanced budget in each fiscal year of operation.

q: An appropriation is an authorization made by:
o: Ordinance directing payment of goods and services from local funds
e: Section 306(b): an authorization by ordinance for payment from local funds under specified conditions or purposes.

q: Economic enterprises of the barangay are accounted for in:
o: A special account in the General Fund
e: Section 313: the LGU maintains a special account in the General Fund for economic enterprises.

q: The executive budget must be submitted to the sanggunian not later than:
e: Section 318: the local chief executive submits the budget not later than the sixteenth of October.

q: The sanggunian must enact the annual budget:
o: On or before the end of the current fiscal year
Within 90 days of the next year
e: Section 319: enactment on or before the end of the current fiscal year.

q: A supplemental budget takes effect:
o: Upon approval or on the date fixed therein
At the start of next year
e: Section 320: the annual budget takes effect at the start of the calendar year; supplemental upon approval.

q: After the executive budget is submitted, a supplemental budget may NOT be enacted EXCEPT when:
o: Funds are available, new revenue sources exist, or in public calamity
e: Section 321 limits supplemental budgets to those three circumstances.

q: Unexpended appropriations revert to the general fund surplus at year-end, except:
e: Section 322: capital outlay appropriations continue until fully spent, reverted or the project is completed.

q: If the sanggunian fails to enact the budget, the budget of the preceding year is deemed:
e: Section 323: the ordinance of the preceding year is deemed reenacted, only for specified items.

q: Appropriations for debt servicing shall not exceed what share of regular income?
e: Section 324(b): debt servicing may not exceed 20% of regular income.

q: Section 325(h) limits discretionary funds to what share of actual basic RPT receipts of the preceding year?
e: Discretionary funds may not exceed 2% of actual receipts from basic real property tax.

q: Under Section 329, the SK gets what share of the barangay general fund?
e: Section 329 sets aside ten percent of the general funds for the SK.

q: The barangay treasurer submits the statement of income and expenditures to the PB on or before:
e: Section 330: on or before September 15, based on the certified statement of the city or municipal treasurer.

q: The responsibility for executing the barangay budget is vested primarily in:
e: Section 332: execution of budgets and accountability are vested primarily in the punong barangay.

q: The sanggunian reviewing a barangay budget has how many days to act?
e: Section 333(a): if no action in 60 days, the ordinance continues in full force and effect.

q: Public money shall not be appropriated or applied for:
e: Section 335 prohibits appropriation for religious or private purposes.

q: Funds are available exclusively for the specific purpose appropriated, except when:
o: Savings augment an item in the same expense class by ordinance authority
e: Section 336 allows augmentation from savings within the same expense class.

q: Disbursements in any local fund may not exceed actual collections plus:
o: Fifty percent of uncollected estimated revenue
e: Section 337 limits disbursements to collections plus 50% of uncollected estimated revenue.

q: No money shall be paid on account of any contract unless:
o: Services have been rendered or goods delivered
e: Section 338: no payment under a contract where no services were rendered or goods delivered.

q: No cash advance may be granted to local officials except:
e: Section 339: cash advances follow rules and regulations prescribed by the COA.

q: Entertainment or reception expenses are prohibited except for:
o: Representation allowances authorized by law or visiting dignitaries
e: Section 343 prohibits entertainment and reception except as allowed by law.

q: The Punong Barangay in the Sangguniang Barangay has what veto power?
e: Section 55(b): the PB, as presiding officer, has no veto power.

q: The presiding officer votes only:
e: Section 49(a): the presiding officer votes only to break a tie.

q: Ordinances enacted by the Sangguniang Barangay, upon approval by a majority of all members, are:
e: Section 54(c): upon approval by the majority of all members, signed by the Punong Barangay.

q: The sanggunian may not hold how many sessions in a single day?
e: Section 52(c): no two sessions, regular or special, may be held in a single day.

q: The Secretary posts an ordinance not later than how many days after approval?
e: Section 59(b): posting within five days after approval.

q: As a general rule, an ordinance takes effect after how many days from posting?
e: Section 59(a): ten days after a copy is posted, unless the ordinance states otherwise.

q: At least what share of the Barangay Development Council are non-government organization representatives?
e: Section 107(a): NGOs constitute not less than one-fourth of the fully organized council.

q: The barangay development council is headed by:
e: Section 107(a): the BDC is headed by the punong barangay.

q: A comprehensive multi-sectoral development plan is mandated by:
e: Section 106 requires each LGU to have a comprehensive multi-sectoral development plan.

q: Under Section 391(a)(10), no increase in sanggunian compensation or honoraria takes effect until:
o: After the full term of all members approving it expires
e: The increase does not take effect until the expiration of the full term of all approving members.

q: The Barangay Treasurer's bond is determined by the SB but not exceeding:
e: Section 395(d): amount determined by the SB not exceeding ₱10,000, premiums paid by the barangay.

q: The Punong Barangay prepares the annual executive budget in coordination with:
e: Section 389(b)(7): the PB, in coordination with the BDC, prepares annual executive and supplemental budgets.

q: The local chief executive submits an annual report to the sanggunian on or before:
e: Section 97: an annual report covering the preceding year is submitted on or before March 31.

q: Enforcing an ordinance or resolution approving a plan after it is declared inoperative may result in:
o: Suspension or dismissal of the official concerned
e: Section 58: attempted enforcement after being declared inoperative is ground for suspension or dismissal.

q: Local government units may contract loans to finance:
o: Public facilities, infrastructure and capital investment projects
e: Section 297 allows loans to finance construction, infrastructure and capital investment projects.

q: Barangay basic services and facilities are enumerated in:
e: Section 17 enumerates basic services and facilities, including the barangay's.
